name: Dunnigan thrust after a held retest
note: Dunnigan's pre-indicator bar grammar, run as a two-sided state machine. An N-bar low anchors a long setup; the market must leave that low by half an ATR and come back to within a quarter of an ATR of it without losing it (the TEST), or make a lower low and close above the bar midpoint and above the prior close (the CLOSING PRICE REVERSAL); only then does the first UP-THRUST - a higher high AND a higher close - buy. Short is the exact mirror around the N-bar high. Both legs expire if the grammar is not completed in time. Exit is the family's own: the first counter-thrust that also closes beyond the extreme bar of the move, or the initial stop at the tested low. The repeat-thrust pyramiding in the source is NOT implemented - the shared harness adds by ATR distance, which is a different mechanism, and faking it would test something else.
source: William Dunnigan, 'One-Way Formula for Trading in Stocks and Commodities' (1954), and his earlier Thrust Method; the clearest modern restatement of the thrust definition (higher high plus higher close), the 'test of the low', the closing price reversal and the repeat-signal rule is in Perry J. Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods', in the chapter on event-driven trends. Dunnigan's original tolerances were stated in points for 1950s commodity contracts, so the harvesting agent pinned them to ATR fractions and bar counts to make the rule symbol-agnostic.
